correctness.rationale: A forced edge must occur on every shortest path between a selected pair. Cartesian coordinate-interleaving shows only same-fiber pairs can force edges, so every C_m fiber needs 3 monitors (all vertices if m=3,4). For m<=n, selecting R+floor(mj/n) in column j gives exactly 3n points. The row maximum circular gap is <=ceil(floor((m-1)/3)*n/m)+1<n/2 for n>=13; the 36 smaller dimension pairs leave exactly (5,6),(7,8), for which RESULT.md supplies explicit 3-per-column arrays with row and column gaps strictly below half-cycle. Thus every edge is forced and 3n meets the fiber lower bound. Independent newly written checker examined 1,235 5<=m<=30, m<=n<=64 pairs and all 36 arithmetic cases. These checks corroborate the all-dimensional inequality, not replace it.
